sources.title: Angels: Reconsidering the Septuagint Reading of Deuteronomy33:2
sources.author: John R. Gilhooly
sources.scope_read: Complete article pp155–159; rendered pp155–156 checked for Hebrew/Greek glyphs
sources.finding: Defends Greek angels through literary context and a tentative Sabean warriors cognate, while acknowledging the translator-knowledge objection. Reports the fire-flew analysis and challenges contraction against Deuteronomy28:49. Later Jewish interpretation is not a chronological cause of early Greek wording.
sources.limit: Authorial argument, not demonstrated Hebrew etymology or a new direct manuscript reading. Its qere characterization is not a reason to erase the actual Masoretic reading tradition. Cited works were not thereby consulted.

B.support: Formally preserves singular abstract qodesh and does not impose angels
B.objection: Counting holiness obscures the likely quality relationship and entities in the poetic scene; an English calque is not automatically faithful ambiguity

C.support: Verse3 mentions his holy ones, and the selected Latin supports holy entities
C.objection: Makes the implied entities explicit where the Hebrew noun itself is holiness; heavenly versus human referent is still unsettled, and Greek Kades is not direct support for this noun rendering

A.support: Quality-genitive rendering keeps holy character and vast numbers without requiring a particular class of beings; no letters, vowels or morphology change
A.objection: Myriads is somewhat elevated English and the adjective does not resolve every possible genitive construal; disclose the close abstract gloss and holy-ones interpretation

root_assessment.holy_phrase_outcome: Provisional preference for A, with the abstract close gloss and holy-ones interpretation disclosed; not proof of heavenly attendants

D.support: Direct Masoretic reading tradition splits fire/law; Sinai and explicit Torah in verse4 permit a law association, and selected Latin supports it
D.objection: Dat vocabulary is unusual in this setting; traditional coherence is not original-priority proof. Holy/angelic and theophanic-fire context admits other readings

E.support: Fire proceeding from the divine hand fits theophanic light/fire imagery; Habakkuk3:3–5 shares Paran and imagery from the hand
E.objection: Needs an alternative contracted-verb analysis, not an ordinary equivalent of the qere noun. Deuteronomy28:49 preserves aleph in a related flying verb, although a different inflected form is not a categorical disproof. The full proponent argument was unavailable

F.support: Actual selected Greek attestation; holy companions and literary context offer a serious textual/interpretive explanation, not merely assumed angelizing
F.objection: The cognate proposal and gloss relation do not establish exact Hebrew wording. A versional interpretation could explain it without a different Hebrew source; importing it would require declared source interpretation, not a silent hybrid

root_assessment.final_colon_outcome: Historical source-meaning priority held unresolved. Retain D only provisionally in the pinned WLC/qere-based English while disclosing serious fire and Greek alternatives; do not declare D the earliest wording
root_assessment.chronology_effect: Greek antiquity warrants serious consideration, but no securely dated decisive direct-Hebrew tail or uniquely distinguishing retroversion was established here. Removing the modest chronological preference leaves both outcomes unchanged; no modern edition dates are used as manuscript dates
root_assessment.attestation_vs_priority: Published selected Greek/Latin and WLC wording are securely identifiable in the inspected editions. Original meaning and source priority remain unresolved; DSS tail supply contributes no discriminating support

independent_comparison.actual_scope: Complete method/doctrine, actual WLC33:1–5,28:49 and Hab3:3–5, selected Greek/Latin, relevant BDB sections and complete Gilhooly pp155–159 with rendered images; no canonical YAML/history/contract/assessment access
independent_comparison.holy_phrase_outcome: A provisionally preferred; C a defensible explanatory alternative
independent_comparison.holy_phrase_reason: Qualitative construct meaning can preserve singular holiness language without counting units of an abstraction or imposing an angel/human identity. C makes the contextual beings explicit and reduces the visible noun distinction from verse3; B is a useful close gloss but a misleading running-English abstraction
independent_comparison.final_colon_outcome: Source priority held; D acceptable only conditional on retaining the Masoretic qere
independent_comparison.final_colon_reason: F represents attested Greek but could be interpretive elucidation; E fits imagery but needs a selected verbal/contraction analysis; D has direct qere and local law context but difficult lexical/syntactic compression. Latin in dextera does not support every detail of D
independent_comparison.countercase: A is compressed and makes quality relation explicit; D uses supplied came/adjectival fiery. Deut28:49's retained aleph in a different form cannot categorically disprove proposed contraction
independent_comparison.chronology_sensitivity: Removing modest chronological tilt leaves both outcomes unchanged
